candidates.name: Nexus Fulcrum Lateral
candidates.monitor_reason: Cannot yet tell whether the plant lateral is the same pipe as the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center spur in the Great Basin 2028 Expansion (P7860). Staging it could duplicate P7860. The tie to data centers is established, so this is not a threshold failure.
candidates.researcher_notes: The data center tie is solid. A June 17, 2026 application to the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada, reported by the Nevada Independent and New Project Media, asks to build a 510 megawatt gas plant at the edge of the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center. The application says the plant is needed to support expanded development there, including data centers. New Project Media says gas would come through a new lateral connecting to the Great Basin Pipeline system. Neither article names a lateral builder, length, route, or diameter. Two data center operators are involved at the park, but who is developing the plant is not clear. The duplicate question is still open. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission scoping notice for the Great Basin 2028 Expansion (docket PF26-5-000, April 2026) lists about 195 miles of 42-inch pipe and about 15 miles of new 24-inch laterals in six Nevada counties, including Storey County. It does not name the industrial center or any plant. A June 2026 Hoodline article, which is low weight, says the filings include a spur to the industrial center aimed at hyperscale facilities, and says gas plants there have planned completion dates of Nov. 1, 2028. No source I could read links the Nexus Fulcrum plant to that spur, and none says the plant lateral is a separate pipe. Searches did not find the Nevada commission docket 26-06016 filings or any Great Basin document naming the plant as a shipper or delivery point. The plant is a single-customer plant that starts construction in 2027, while the spur is due in service in late 2028, so the spur is a plausible supply path. Same pipe is the more likely reading. The documents that would settle it are the Great Basin 2028 Expansion application or resource reports in the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission eLibrary (delivery points in Storey County), or the gas supply section of the Nexus Fulcrum plant application in the Nevada commission docket. If the spur turns out to serve this plant, class it as matched to P7860 and treat it as a data center tag lead for that row. If it is a separate pipe, add it as a new row under the parent system name 'Great Basin Gas Transmission Company Pipeline System' with segment name 'Nexus Fulcrum Lateral', status proposed, Fuel Gas, Nevada, Storey County, owner blank, no route, data center yes. Owner is blank because no builder is named. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 0 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s) -> no.

candidates.name: Stratos Project Ruby Pipeline Lateral
candidates.monitor_reason: no pipeline project described: sources say the campus would use unused capacity on the existing Ruby Pipeline, which crosses the site, and none describes a new lateral, supply line or named tap. It would become a project when a Tallgrass or Ruby filing, a Utah air permit application, a development agreement text, or a developer or county document says a line or connection will be built to the campus.
candidates.researcher_notes: This was re-checked under the 2026-10-19 ruling. Location, sponsor and length are no longer required, but a pipeline project still has to be described. None is. A Box Elder County fact sheet lists direct access to the Ruby Pipeline as a selling point of the site. A WyoFile story from May 2026 quotes the developer's co-founder at an April 27 county meeting saying the data center would tap unused capacity on the pipeline that is not under contract. That is use of existing capacity, not new pipe. A Pipeline and Gas Journal story from May 2026 says Ruby is eyed for the project, but its text could not be read past the headline. Third-party listings and press say gas would come through a Tallgrass deal and a connection to Ruby, but none describes a lateral or names a tap, and no Tallgrass notice, federal filing or Utah air permit application was found. A tap or meter station with no new pipe is only added when a filing names it. Do not tag the Ruby Pipeline row (P0248). Earlier work on this lead (Landgate article, ABC4 development agreement documents) is unchanged.

candidates.name: Woodway Hyperscale Data Center Pipeline

values.DataCenterNotes: Woodway's own announcement of September 22, 2026 says the pipeline will give dedicated gas transport capacity to a behind-the-meter power generation project for hyperscale data center development. The customer, the data center and the site are not named. A trade news report from September 2026 repeats this and says the pipeline has an option for extension. Woodway is based in Houston.

candidates.researcher_notes: Woodway Energy Infrastructure announced on September 22, 2026 that it signed definitive agreements to develop, build, own and run a 22-mile, 30-inch gas pipeline. The pipeline gives dedicated capacity to a power plant behind the meter for hyperscale data center development. Service is expected in the first half of 2028, subject to regulatory approvals. This meets the data center add rule: a real pipeline project, described by its developer, that supplies energy to a data center. No existing row matches. The state is inferred, not stated. Woodway's own operating assets page lists only Texas pipelines (Bluebonnet in Bastrop, Colorado, Lee, Fayette and Lavaca counties, Comal County, and Goliad County), and Woodway is an intrastate pipeline operator based in Houston, so Texas is the likely state. A trade news report also says the company's assets are all in Texas. The county, the customer and the data center site were not found in the announcement, trade news or searches, and no Texas Railroad Commission filing for this line was found. The start and end places and the route are blank and the route accuracy is 'no route'. The pipeline name is a working name made from the announcement. The Woodway announcement and the BIC Magazine report are one story reprinted, and the Data Center Dynamics and W Media reports repeat the same release, so none is independent. Confidence is medium. Owner is spelled as the company spells it with its LLC form, and the ownership list has no existing match to reuse.
